No API key, no registration, plain HTTPS.
license_and_commercial_rights: Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY); COMMERCIAL USE IS PERMITTED. Verified 2026-07-25 by reading the publisher's own machine-readable CKAN record rather than trusting data/ACQUISITION_PLAN.md: https://data.ca.gov/api/3/action/package_show?id=cal-itp-gtfs-ingest-pipeline-dataset returns license_id='cc-by', license_title='Creative Commons Attribution', license_url='http://www.opendefinition.org/licenses/cc-by', rights='No restrictions on public use', accessLevel='public', isopen=true, organization='Caltrans'. The commercial-use verdict does not depend on the version: every published CC-BY version (2.5, 3.0, 4.0) grants commercial use. THE VERSION IS NOT PINNED BY THE SOURCE -- the acquisition plan expected the CKAN license field to confirm it and it does not; license_url is the Open Definition's version-agnostic cc-by entry, which itself lists 4.0, 3.0 and 2.5. Licence text Milexium attributes under: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ -- recorded as OUR choice of the current version, not as the publisher's declaration. Required attribution: 'California Integrated Travel Program (Cal-ITP), California Department of Transportation'; contact calitp@dot.ca.gov. PUBLISHER USE NOTE, quoted verbatim from the CKAN notes field: 'Cal-ITP collects the GTFS feeds from a statewide list every night and aggregates it into a statewide table for analysis purposes only. Do not use for trip planner ingestion, rather is meant to be used for statewide analytics and other use cases. Note: These data may or may or may not have passed GTFS-Validation' -- Milexium's use (statewide scheduled-deadhead analytics) is inside that stated intent, and these bytes must NOT be served to a passenger trip planner. SCOPE LIMIT: this grant is Caltrans' over ITS aggregation. The ~200 underlying per-operator feeds keep their own upstream terms; this record does not launder them and is NOT authority to fetch any agency feed directly.
geography: California, statewide -- every operator on Cal-ITP's nightly ingest list
time_coverage: current statewide snapshot; refreshed and republished monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M)
schema_and_format: CSV keyed on (base64_url, agency_id), carrying agency_name, agency_url, agency_timezone. This is the denominator of the headline finding 'how many agencies publish a usable block_id at all'. agency_id is OPTIONAL in GTFS and is blank in single-agency feeds; a blank agency_id in a single-agency feed still identifies exactly one agency, so the derivation treats (base64_url, '') as a valid agency key rather than discarding the feed.
update_frequency: monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M). source_checksum is null -- trust-on-first-use.
canonical_contract: none-yet -- this repo has no canonical Agency/Operator entity and this packet does not invent one. It supplies the human-readable operator identity attached to the derived coverage report, and nothing is stored on a canonical row from it.

quality_tests.name: header_carries_feed_key_and_agency_name
quality_tests.description: the first line contains base64_url and agency_name -- without a name the coverage finding is a list of opaque keys

quality_tests.name: at_least_a_hundred_agencies
quality_tests.description: more than 100 distinct (base64_url, agency_id) pairs, i.e. the statewide assembly rather than a truncated page; the acquisition plan expected ~200 California operators

acceptance_threshold: downloads over plain HTTPS with no credential, is CSV, > 10 KB, header contains base64_url and agency_name, and more than 100 distinct agency rows.
retention_and_deletion: retain: negligible size (~70 KB) and it is the identity layer for every finding in this packet. Reproducible monthly.
